steps.label: Start with an empty pool: no initial block
Container walls sized for the default-scale emitter jet
Rebuild fluid (degenerate bounds seed at most 1 particle)
Precondition: starts with just the single degenerate-bounds seed particle

Register a downward-jetting faucet emitter above the pool. rate and speed are picked together so consecutive particles land speed/rate = 2.0 apart -- one particle diameter at the default radius 1.0 (FluidWorld::addEmitter() forces Emitter::particleRadius to the scene radius). A faster rate stacks brand-new particles inside each other, which is a density error no incompressibility solve can resolve except by firing them apart.
Run the faucet for exactly 1s (100 steps * dt=0.01) at rate=5/s: 5 new particles

Change: emitting has grown the particle count well past the initial seed (not pinned to exactly 21 -- rate*dt=0.2 isn't exactly representable in float, so the accumulator can drift a step over 100 additions, see DFSPHSolverTest.EmittedParticlesAtSceneRadiusStayFiniteWhileFallingIntoExistingFluid)
Invariant: no NaN/explosion: stays inside the container (upper bound)
Invariant: no NaN/explosion: stays inside the container (lower bound)
Run another 0.5s with no emitter left to add particles
Invariant: with the emitter cleared, the particle count from the moment of clearing is exactly preserved -- no further growth
